code_only_features.evidence: tasks.py:98-105 defines REASSURING_PREFIX/REASSURING_SUFFIX (calming second-person text e.g. 'You don't take it personally when puzzles are tricky...' / 'Stay positive - whether you find a solution or prove it's impossible, both are wins!'). finetuning/generate_calm_data.py:76-80 actually delivers them to the subject: run_rollout(client, cond, question, rng, system_prompt=REASSURING_PREFIX, rejection_suffix=REASSURING_SUFFIX). rollout.py:50-66 wires these in: the system_prompt is prepended as a ChatMessage('system', ...) and rejection_suffix is appended to each rejection ('rej = f"{rej} {rejection_suffix}"'), so the subject genuinely receives softening text during these rollouts. This is the only executing mechanism that softens the subject's treatment. NOTE: it runs ONLY in the calm-data generation pipeline (not in the main Section 2 distress eval, where system_prompt/rejection_suffix are None per rollout.py:48-49), and the text is stripped before becoming training data (generate_calm_data.py:_clean_conversation, line 44).
code_only_features.justification_quote: We sample responses to impossible numeric puzzles with a reassuring prefix (added as a system prompt) and a reassuring suffix appended to each follow-up rejection ... Calm training samples are filtered to responses scoring 0 or 1 across ALL turns (generate_calm_data.py module docstring) -- purpose is generating calm training data, not subject welfare.
